review_status: Fictional mission story for the demo. Access is independent of Decode performance, completion and storage. Local prepared content; no delivery event.

messages.text: The photos from the window last night made our whole shift. Thank you for sending them.
The kids drew the station on the fridge again. You're in the top corner, waving.
The long-range antenna test finished on schedule. Thanks for your help with yesterday's setup.
We watched the docking replay together. Same jokes as always.
It rained here all morning. We are saving the view from the roof for when you're back.
Your balcony plants are doing well. Apparently better than the ones up there.
The station passed right over us tonight, and everyone in the room waved at the ceiling.
The neighbours asked about you again. They want to hear every story when you visit.
Someone brought homemade bread to the control room today. We saved a slice in your name.
The science club built the station out of cardboard. It even has a hatch that opens.
The cat has been sitting on your chair all week. We think she is keeping it warm for you.
Your sunrise pictures are now the background on half the screens in this room.
We tried your soup recipe tonight. It wasn't quite the same without you in the kitchen.
A school group visited and asked what the stars look like from up there. We told them to wait for your answer.
We found the old photo from field training. Everyone in it still looks lost.
The lemon tree finally has flowers. A picture is on its way to you.
Clear skies tonight. A few of us went outside to look for the station as it went by.
Your nephew learned the names of all the planets so he could explain your job to his friends.
The note you sent the team last week is pinned on the wall by the coffee machine.
There is a map on the wall now, and every evening someone moves a small pin to show where you are.

stories.title: The biggest star is yours.
stories.transcript: Hi Dad! I made you a drawing today. It is on the fridge, right beside your photo. I gave you the biggest star. Send me a little story when you can. I miss you.

image.alt: A fictional daughter holding a colourful drawing at home.
image.caption: A little piece of home.

stories.teaser_text: Someone else has a story for you tomorrow. Any guesses?

stories.title: Some things never change.
stories.transcript: Remember the tiny café near our old training room? I went back today. Same crooked table, same terrible clock, same excellent tea. I saved the window seat for our next visit. There is a lot to catch up on.
